cases.name: 2024 Red Sea Maritime Chokepoint & Conflict Crisis
cases.affected_country: Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb / European Ports
cases.severity_rationale: Drone and anti-ship missile attacks on commercial vessels near Bab el-Mandeb forced major container liners (Maersk, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd) to divert around the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10 to 14 sailing days and 400% container spot freight increases between Asia and Europe. Combines armed geopolitical conflict with severe logistics container delays.
cases.source_org: UNCTAD (United Nations Trade & Development) / Reuters / IMF PortWatch
cases.notes_on_facts: UNCTAD reported an 82% year-over-year decline in Suez Canal container ship transits by mid-January 2024. Represents multi-signal compounding of security conflict and maritime transit disruption.

events.headline: Commercial container carriers suspend Red Sea voyages following missile strikes on merchant ships
events.summary: Armed attacks on commercial shipping vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait prompt leading ocean container carriers to halt Red Sea transit due to direct security risks.

events.headline: Cape of Good Hope container rerouting adds 12 days transit and triggers acute port arrival delays
events.summary: Ocean container lines routing vessels around Africa report transit extensions of 10 to 14 days, creating equipment shortages and vessel arrival clustering at North European terminals.

cases.name: 2021 Suez Canal Obstruction (Ever Given Grounding)
cases.severity_rationale: Ultra-large container ship Ever Given ran aground and completely obstructed the Suez Canal for 6 days, halting approximately $9.6 billion per day of maritime freight between Asia and Europe (~12% of global trade). European ports (Rotterdam, Antwerp, Hamburg) faced container dwell spikes and berth congestion for weeks.
cases.source_org: Lloyd's List Intelligence / Suez Canal Authority / BBC News
cases.notes_on_facts: Canal was physically obstructed from March 23 to March 29, 2021. 422 vessels were stranded in queue. Port congestion across Northern European container hubs peaked 10 to 14 days after refloating.

events.headline: Container ship Ever Given runs aground, blocking all Suez Canal maritime transit
events.summary: The 20,000 TEU Ever Given container vessel has grounded diagonally across the southern single-lane section of the Suez Canal, completely halting northbound and southbound convoys between Europe and Asia.

cases.name: 2024 Typhoon Gaemi (Carina) Extreme Weather Disruption
cases.severity_rationale: Category 4 equivalent super typhoon with sustained winds over 115 mph (gusts >140 mph) and over 1,000 mm of torrential rainfall in mountainous Taiwan. Financial markets, government offices, international flights, and seaport operations at Kaohsiung and Keelung were shut down for two consecutive days. Science parks operated on emergency protocols.
cases.source_org: Central Weather Administration (Taiwan) / JTWC / Bloomberg Markets
cases.notes_on_facts: Nationwide disaster response declared July 24-25, 2024. Container ports suspended crane operations, coastal cargo vessels sheltered, and semiconductor fabs operated with essential personnel only.

events.headline: Super Typhoon Gaemi makes landfall in Taiwan with torrential rains and 140 mph wind gusts
events.summary: Severe tropical cyclone Gaemi lashes northern and eastern Taiwan, triggering widespread flooding, power disruptions, and mandatory closure of ports, financial institutions, and manufacturing operations.

cases.name: 2024 US East & Gulf Coast ILA Dockworkers Port Strike
cases.severity_rationale: 45,000 dockworkers represented by the International Longshoremen's Association (ILA) struck across 36 container ports along the US Atlantic and Gulf Coasts, halting approximately 50% of total US maritime ocean import/export trade. Shippers faced immediate component delays and ocean carriers implemented emergency congestion surcharges of $1,000 to $3,000 per container.
cases.source_org: United States Maritime Alliance (USMX) / ILA / CNBC Supply Chain
cases.notes_on_facts: First coastwide ILA strike since 1977 commenced Oct 1, 2024. A tentative wage agreement suspended the strike late Oct 3, but anchor queues of dozens of container vessels required 2 to 3 weeks to clear backlogged import cargo.

events.headline: Dockworkers strike shuts 36 ports along US East and Gulf Coasts from Maine to Texas
events.summary: Master contract expiration triggers full labor walkout across 14 major port authorities, halting container gantry cranes and roll-on/roll-off automotive terminals.

events.headline: Vessel anchor queues expand off Savannah and New York, threatening manufacturing component shortages
events.summary: Marine terminals report growing queues of container vessels at anchor outside East Coast ports, with logistics operators warning of inventory dwell and electronic component delivery delays.
